html:
An East Germanic people who founded a kingdom in the Rhône valley in the 5th century and gave their name to Burgundy. The map shows them in 400 and 500 in what is now eastern France and western Switzerland.

In the early 5th century they set up a kingdom on the Rhine around Worms, inside the Roman frontier. In 436 the Roman general Aetius destroyed it with the help of Hun troops, killing thousands, a disaster remembered centuries later in the German epic the Nibelungenlied. Aetius then settled the survivors in Sapaudia, the land around Lake Geneva.

From there they built a new kingdom centred on Lyon and Geneva. King Gundobad, who ruled from about 480 to 516, issued a law code, the Lex Burgundionum, with rules for Burgundians and Romans living side by side. The kings were mostly Arian Christians ruling Catholic Romans. Squeezed between the Ostrogoths and the Franks, the kingdom fell to the Franks in 534.
sum: An East Germanic people who founded a kingdom in the Rhône valley in the 5th century and gave their name to Burgundy. The map shows them in 400 and 500 in what is now eastern France and western Switzerland.
